exceptionApproval.scope: Release-scoped engineering compliance risk acceptance for the four disclosed missing upstream MIT license/attribution bodies in the Personal Research Workbench 0.0.6 Windows x64 candidate only. This does not assert that missing upstream notices were recovered or that no additional notice exists.
basis: Official exact-version npm responses declare MIT for all four packages; retained response bodies, extracted declarations, bounded search results and original installed README documents were independently checked against their recorded hashes.
The SPDX MIT template remains explicitly marked standard-template-not-upstream, with its placeholder unfilled. No author is inferred to be the copyright holder and no upstream wording is synthesized.

All 121 exact crate name/version/checksum records match the retained source Cargo.lock and carry archiveVerified assertions. The reviewer independently checked the lock/report correspondence and retained source/notice hashes, but did not re-download archives, compile native code or establish binary reproducibility.

The conservative Windows/build dependency closure has zero reported license-body or supported-selection gaps. Original selected MIT, BSL-1.0, Zlib, Apache-2.0 and ISC bodies are retained. The exact unicode-ident compound selects MIT AND Unicode-3.0 and retains both bodies. Nonselected alternatives or exceptions are not thereby approved.
The acknowledged clipboard_rs upstream MIT notice is retained at its recorded fixed revision; exact equivalence to modified vendored sources is not asserted.

Independent read-only checks verified 254 content-addressed text files, 520 referenced text digests, all 121 stored license selections and seven unsupported-expression rejection cases. The offline generator check reproduced the frozen evidence with exit 1 solely for these four not-yet-approved exceptions.
conditions: Preserve the complete frozen disclosure, original available notices, content-addressed license texts, chosen-license evidence and standard-template labels in the actual packaged resources/legal/0.0.6 payload.
Preserve Electron and Chromium distribution notices in the actual Windows package and independently verify the final payload; this record alone does not establish their presence.
Retain all 15 other-target gaps and the Apple SDK derivation caveat. No macOS or other-target license completeness or distribution approval is granted.

Any change to either bound evidence document, the four exact versions or the native dependency provenance requires a new review. This acceptance does not carry forward automatically to another release.
limitations: Missing upstream copyright/notice bodies remain a disclosed legal and attribution risk. This is not legal advice, legal clearance, a copyright warranty or a cryptographic reviewer signature.
The inventory is a conservative source/dependency superset, not an exhaustive binary SBOM, enabled-feature proof, linker audit or source-to-binary reproducibility attestation.

Actual NSIS package identity, installation, restart, persistence, reinstall, migration, uninstall, signing, update behavior and online service acceptance remain separate gates. This record does not approve publication.
Independent legal/security approval is separate from this mechanical gate.
SPDX standard templates do not reconstruct missing upstream copyright/notice text; disclosed exceptions require an explicit release-scoped independent acceptance record.
An approval file is an auditable decision record, not cryptographic proof of reviewer identity and not legal advice.
Native/bundled subcomponents are covered only to the extent identified by upstream package notices; this is not an exhaustive binary/SBOM audit.
Electron/Chromium licenses must remain in the packaged distribution.
Official npm provenance metadata is not claimed as independently signature-verified.
